title: Fractional vortices in a spin-isotropic spiral spin liquid
authors: Cecilie Glittum, Han Yan, Johannes Reuther
abstract: Spiral spin liquids are magnetic states whose classical ground-state manifold consists of planar incommensurate spin spirals with wave vectors lying on a continuous ring or surface in reciprocal space. The resulting subextensive degeneracy suppresses magnetic long-range order and gives rise to liquid-like behavior. Despite numerous material realizations and theoretical investigations, the structure of low-temperature spin configurations of spin-isotropic Heisenberg spiral spin liquids has remained poorly understood. Here, we classify and characterize the classical topological defects supported by these systems. We uncover a rich family of vortex types involving concerted windings of spin directions, spiral-plane normals, and wave-vector orientations, yielding a $\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ classification. Remarkably, the elementary defects are half-vortices carrying fractional $2π$ windings in both spin and momentum space and obey fusion rules resembling to those of Ising anyons. Large-scale classical simulations of a square-lattice spiral spin liquid reveal that these vortices are dense in the spiral-spin-liquid regime, and bind tightly below an order-by-disorder phase transition, eventually fusing to vacuum.
summary: This theoretical work classifies the topological defects in spiral spin liquids by mapping the system's order parameter space to a $\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ structure. The key finding is that the vortices carry fractional charges and obey fusion rules analogous to Ising anyons. This provides a deep mathematical understanding of the emergent quasi-particle physics in these complex magnetic materials.
main_problem: The paper aims to classify and characterize the classical topological defects (vortices) present in spin-isotropic Heisenberg spiral spin liquids.
main_result: The system supports a rich family of vortices classified by a $\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ structure, where elementary defects are half-vortices resembling Ising anyons in their fusion rules.
method: The classification relies on analyzing the first homotopy group of the order parameter space, $\pi_1(\text{U}(1) \times \text{SO}(3)/\mathbb{Z}_2)$, and developing multiplicative fusion rules for the topological charges.
model_or_system: The system is a spin-isotropic Heisenberg model on a square lattice, whose classical ground state is a planar incommensurate spin spiral. The low-energy physics is described by an order parameter manifold $M = S^1_{\hat{q}} \times \text{SO}(3) / \langle\gamma\rangle$.
key_observables: Topological charges $(u, v)$, spin-wave entropy per site ($s$), and the $\mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}_2$ classification of vortices.
important_parameters: The coupling constants $J_1, J_2, J_3$ define the spiral state; the analysis distinguishes between fractional ($u=\pm 1$) and non-fractional vortices.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a well-defined local low-energy spiral texture and uses continuum limit approximations for the defect analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the definition of couplings, planar spiral states, momentum vortices, and the mathematical structure of the topological indices $u$ and $v$ used for classification.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical system and its ground state to generalizing the wave vector definition for Heisenberg spins. It then systematically develops the topological classification using homotopy theory, culminating in the derivation of the multiplicative fusion rules for the vortex charges.
why_interesting: The connection between topological defects (vortices) and anyon statistics (Ising anyons) in a magnetically ordered, yet liquid-like, state is highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phenomena in frustrated magnets.
